- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.33) in recent days, model tends to underestimate; increase forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >70% from prior 30d mean), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above peak or adjust downward by 2–3 points.
- Model consistently underestimates true values in early 30d window (first 5–7 days) — apply upward bias of +1–2 points for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or neutral sentiment, model exhibits mean-reversion bias — forecast should be adjusted toward recent 5–7 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after a peak, model often fails to correct — apply downward bias of -1–3 points for days following peak.
- Model tends to ignore sentiment shifts in first 3–5 days — if sentiment changes from negative to positive, adjust forecast upward by +1–2 points after day 5.
